patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Drip and Kit share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Drip and Kit share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Drip only if your buying job matches “Ecommerce CRM/email platform with behavior-driven automation and contact-tier pricing from” rather than Kit's shape. Choose Kit only if your buying job matches “Creator and newsletter ESP (formerly ConvertKit) with landing pages, automations, and digi” rather than Drip's shape. Workflow advantage: Drip leans ecommerce-email; Kit leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Drip and Kit share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Drip is Ecommerce CRM/email platform with behavior-driven automation and contact-tier pricing from $39/mo.; Kit is Creator and newsletter ESP (formerly ConvertKit) with landing pages, automations, and digital product selling..
- Company-size focus: Drip (small-business, mid-market) vs Kit (micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Drip-leaning ecommerce-email vs Kit-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Drip — No forever-free plan — trial-only entry from $39/mo; Kit — Free Newsletter plan limits automations vs Creator/Pro.

Limitations — Drip: No forever-free plan — trial-only entry from $39/mo; Contact-tier pricing rises as the store list grows; Kit: Free Newsletter plan limits automations vs Creator/Pro; Paid pricing scales with subscribers.

Poor-fit cases: Drip is a poor fit when that limitation bites: No forever-free plan — trial-only entry from $39/mo · Kit is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Free Newsletter plan limits automations vs Creator/Pro · Avoid Drip if you actually need Kit's motion (Creator and newsletter ESP (formerly ConvertKit) with landing pages, automations)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
